lessons.title: Non-Fiction: Our World
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to retrieve facts about the world's continents from a non-fiction text.
success_criteria: I can find a fact about a continent.
I can answer a question using the text.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model reading a simple non-fiction text about the continents.
lessons.independent_task: Children read an extract and answer retrieval questions about continents.
key_questions: Where did you find that fact?

differentiation.greater_depth: Answer in full sentences using text evidence

lessons.assessment_notes: Note non-fiction retrieval skill — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Look at a world map or globe at home if available.

lessons.title: Number Recap: Counting to 20 and Beyond
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to count confidently to 20 and beyond as a consolidation check.
success_criteria: I can count to 20.
I can count beyond 20 with support.
lessons.starter_activity: Count around the class to 20 and beyond.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Recap counting strategies covered across the year, extending informally beyond 20.
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a counting consolidation activity, extending to 30 where confident.
lessons.assessment_notes: End-of-topic consolidation check on counting fluency — evidence for MATHS.N1.
lessons.plenary: Class count together as far as everyone can go.
lessons.home_link: Practise counting as high as you can with your family.

lessons.title: Introducing the Seven Continents
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to name the seven continents.
success_criteria: I can name 4+ continents.
I can find them on a world map.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce all seven continents (Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, South America, Australia/Oceania, Antarctica) on a world map.
lessons.independent_task: Children label all seven continents on a world map outline.

differentiation.greater_depth: Label all 7 and name an animal/feature from each

lessons.assessment_notes: Note locational knowledge of continents — evidence for GEOG.1.
lessons.home_link: Find the continents on a map or globe together.

lessons.title: Writing About a Continent
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write factual sentences about a chosen continent.
success_criteria: I can write a fact about a continent.
I can use a capital letter and full stop.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model writing a factual sentence about a continent (e.g. Antarctica is very cold).
lessons.independent_task: Children write 2-3 factual sentences about a chosen continent.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note factual writing progress — evidence for ENG.W2/W3.
lessons.home_link: Tell your family a fact about a continent.

lessons.title: Comparing Sizes of Continents
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to compare and order continents by approximate size.
success_criteria: I can say which continent looks bigger.
I can order 3 continents by size.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model comparing continent sizes using a world map, discussing biggest (Asia) to smallest (Australia).
lessons.independent_task: Children order continent shape cut-outs from biggest to smallest.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note size comparison and ordering skill applied to geography — evidence for MATHS.MEA.
lessons.home_link: Compare sizes of countries or continents on a map together.

lessons.title: Animals of Each Continent
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to match an animal to the continent it is associated with.
success_criteria: I can name an animal from a continent.
I can match it correctly on a map.
lessons.starter_activity: Guess which continent an animal picture might be from.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss animals associated with each continent (e.g. lions in Africa, pandas in Asia, penguins in Antarctica).
lessons.independent_task: Children match animal picture cards to their continent on a world map.
key_questions: Which continent is this animal from?

differentiation.greater_depth: Match 7+ pairs and add an extra fact

lessons.assessment_notes: Note locational knowledge linked to animals — evidence for GEOG.1/SCI.ANI links.
lessons.home_link: Look up an animal from a continent you haven't studied before.

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading Continent Names
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read continent names and related words.
success_criteria: I can blend and read continent words.
I can read a sentence about a continent.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce/reinforce a grapheme, blending simplified continent-related words (e.g. 'cold', 'hot', 'land').
lessons.independent_task: Children read themed word and sentence cards.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics application — evidence for ENG.R1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading continent-related words over the week.

lessons.title: Comparing Temperature Across Continents
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to compare temperatures in different continents/climates.
success_criteria: I can say which place is hotter/colder.
I can order 3 places by temperature.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model comparing typical temperatures in different continents (Antarctica vs Africa) using simple data.
lessons.independent_task: Children order continent temperature cards from coldest to hottest.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note temperature comparison applied to geography — evidence for MATHS.MEA.
lessons.home_link: Compare temperatures of different places you know.

lessons.title: Climate Around the World
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe different climates found around the world.
success_criteria: I can describe a hot climate.
I can describe a cold climate.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap hot/cold places from earlier learning.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss different climate types (tropical, polar, desert, temperate) simply, with examples.
lessons.independent_task: Children match climate descriptions to continent pictures, recording their matching.
resources_needed: Climate description and continent picture cards
key_questions: Which continent might have this climate?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note climate vocabulary and geographical reasoning — evidence for GEOG.2.
lessons.home_link: Talk about the climate where you live.

lessons.title: Continent Quiz Show
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer and ask questions about the continents in a quiz format.
success_criteria: I can answer a question about a continent.
I can ask a question about a continent.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap all continents and facts learned.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss how to ask a clear quiz question.
lessons.independent_task: Children play a continent quiz game in teams, asking and answering questions.
resources_needed: Continent fact cards for quiz questions
key_questions: Which continent has the most animals you know?
Can you ask us a question?

differentiation.greater_depth: Create and ask original quiz questions

lessons.assessment_notes: Note cumulative geographical knowledge and questioning skill — evidence for ENG.SL1/GEOG.1.
lessons.home_link: Quiz your family on the continents.

lessons.title: Continent Word Problems
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to solve addition/subtraction word problems using a continents context.
success_criteria: I can solve an addition problem.
I can solve a subtraction problem.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model solving word problems using a continents/animals context (e.g. animals seen on a trip).
lessons.independent_task: Children solve continent-themed word problems, showing working.
lessons.assessment_notes: Record word problem solving skill — evidence for MATHS.N2.
lessons.home_link: Make up a word problem about animals or places for your family.

lessons.title: Where Would You Like to Visit?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to say which continent they would like to visit and why.
success_criteria: I can name a continent I'd like to visit.
I can give a reason why.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap all continents studied this week.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss giving a reason for a preference using continent facts learned.
lessons.independent_task: Children draw and write about a continent they'd like to visit and why.
key_questions: Which continent would you like to visit?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note application of the week's geographical knowledge to a personal opinion — evidence for GEOG.1.
lessons.home_link: Discuss with your family which continent you'd like to visit.

lessons.title: Continents Quiz: Reading Comprehension
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer comprehension questions about the continents.
success_criteria: I can answer a retrieval question.
I can answer an inference question.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a summary passage about the continents, modelling retrieval and inference questions.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer a mix of retrieval and inference questions about the passage.
key_questions: Why do animals suit their continent's climate?

differentiation.support: Answer retrieval questions with text pointing

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension progress — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Quiz your family on the continents you learned about.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Comparing Size and Temperature
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply comparing size, temperature, and word problem skills.
success_criteria: I can compare sizes.
I can compare temperatures.
I can solve a word problem.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of the week's comparison and word problem learning.
lessons.independent_task: Children rotate through 2 stations: size/temperature comparison, word problems.
key_questions: How did you solve this problem?
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 27 maths observations for each child — evidence for MATHS.MEA/N2.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining both skills.

lessons.title: Continents Topic Recap and Celebration
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key facts about the world's continents learned this week.
success_criteria: I can name the seven continents.
I can name an animal and climate from one continent.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss synthesising the week's learning about continents.
lessons.independent_task: Contribute to a class 'Seven Continents' display combining maps, animal matching, and quiz facts from the week.
key_questions: What have we learned about the continents?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note synthesis of the week's learning — evidence for GEOG.1/GEOG.2.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned about the continents with your family.
